note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a NOR 7, 8; A06b NOR 7, 8; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: UDI (Norwegian Directorate of Immigration), "Dual citizenship"; UDI, "Sufficient income for reduced residence time when applying for citizenship" (published 24.06.2021, last changed 05.12.2025). It confirmed renunciation and loss on taking another citizenship. It was silent on the years of residence, birth in the territory and descent, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Norway, 2024
sources.said: Person has resided in Norway for a total of 8 years in the last 11 years with residence or work permits of at least 1 year duration, or, if person has sufficient income (established by  regulation) according to a tax settlement, for a total of 6 years in the last 10 years with residence or work permits of at least 1 year duration. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born to a citizen. ... No provision ... No provision

sources.title: UDI (Norwegian Directorate of Immigration), "Dual citizenship"
sources.said: From 1 January 2020, it is allowed to have one or more citizenships in addition to a Norwegian citizenship. ... You do not have to inform Norwegian authorities that you wish to keep your previous citizenship.

sources.title: UDI, "Sufficient income for reduced residence time when applying for citizenship" (published 24.06.2021, last changed 05.12.2025)
sources.said: If you have sufficient income the required residence time for Norwegian citizenship is less. If you have sufficient income, you are required to have resided in Norway six out of the last ten years.
